short_title: Hautefort to Bellièvre, Grenoble 1584 (fr. 15567 ff. 158-164; fr. 15568 ff. 207-208)
writer: Jean de Bellièvre, sieur de Hautefort, président at the Parlement de Grenoble (d. 25 Sept 1584)
recipient: Pomponne de Bellièvre, his brother, counsellor of Henri III
date: March 1584 (ff. 158-161, clear closing 'de Grenoble ... mars 1584'); fr. 15568 ff. 207-208 Apr-Dec 1584, day not read
matters: Six to eight pages of cipher from the head of the Dauphiné parlement to the king's counsellor in the year of the Lesdiguières wars and of Anjou's death; the unread text is the writer's confidential report from Grenoble
matters_src: PRIMARY: Gallica fr. 15567 https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b90639282 (f. 161 signature 'Hautefort', per Tomokiyo's crop); SECONDARY: https://data.bnf.fr/12539480/jean_de_bellievre/ (Jean de Bellièvre-Hautefort, président, Grenoble, 1524-1584)
not_taken: FAIL as a key-building item: Tomokiyo has published the key. 'Hautefort's Cipher', reconstructed from ff. 158, 160 and fr. 15568 f. 207, https://cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/henryiii.htm (image henryiii_Hautefort.png, saved to sources/cache/cross/2839/). By eye: about 39 letter signs give every letter a-x at least one value, with 2-4 homophones for a, c, d, h, n, o, p, s; y and z have no value; there is 1 null and 4 word signs (vous=12, nous=20, par, que). Not in line/taken-2026-11-19.tsv; profile grep (Hautefort, Bellièvre, 15567, 15568) finds no target, only mentions in mercoeur1587 and nevers1588. No reading of the text is published.
searches: WebSearch 'Hautefort Bellièvre 1584 chiffre Grenoble déchiffrement' (no reading; it turned up a lead to a Grenoble colloquium talk by Jacques de Monts de Savasse on 'son déchiffrement', subject unknown, https://www.arcsi.fr/doc/Tant/420.pdf, not opened); catalogue vetting of 15 Nov (GL.htm, DECODE dumps, known.py: nothing). Not checked: the ARCSI PDF, Gallica full text, the Lasry-Biermann-Tomokiyo papers
h_median: 25.0 (f. 158), 28 (f. 207); by eye signs are 60-100 px tall at full size (crop_top.jpg); line/sign_height.py
pair: Interlined decipherment on f. 158 is a few short runs of small letters over about four of 31 lines (seen on the 1400 px preview and a full-size crop); Tomokiyo reports the same for f. 160
pair_signs: under 100 interlined letters on f. 158 by eye; not counted
neighbour_keys: Tomokiyo's Hautefort table itself (same writer, same year; henryiii.htm). Same page: Maygnieulx's Cipher (ff. 162, 194), Aubeterre's, Matignon-1
second_passage: yes: ff. 159-161, the passages on ff. 162-164, fr. 15568 ff. 207-208 (2 pages x about 36 lines x about 35 signs, entirely cipher). That is well over 3,000 signs
design: A homophonic letter substitution, one sign per letter (digits 1, 3, 4, Greek-like and invented forms, ff, B, A), with a few digit signs for words. Two-digit signs on f. 158 (13, 14, 15, 17, 35) are not in Tomokiyo's table and are probably more word signs
failed_gate: not_taken (published key: a known-key reading, another job)
notes: A strong known-key reading job: the images are huge (h about 25-28 px by script, 60+ px by eye), the table is near-complete for letters, and about 8 pages are unread. What is left after the table: the word signs, y and z, and any missing homophones. Heavy show-through from the versos on f. 158 and f. 207. f. 162 may be in Maygnieulx's cipher rather than Hautefort's (Tomokiyo); check before treating ff. 162-164 as the same system.

short_title: Paris despatches to Cardinal Caetani and the Pope, 1590-91 (AAV Francia 32, DECODE R5613-14, R5617-21)
writer: Filippo Sega, Bishop of Piacenza, in Paris with Legate Caetani (the outside repo identifies the sender of R5612, R5615 and R5616 as Sega)
recipient: Cardinal Enrico Caetani / the papal Secretariat (dockets 1591)
matters: Papal despatches from League Paris after the siege of 1590, at the turning point of the papacy's support for the League; the unread passages are the ciphered political core
matters_src: PRIMARY: DECODE https://de-crypt.org/decrypt-web/RecordsView/5613 (record, login needed); SCHOLARLY: Penzi, 'La Ligue et la papauté dans l'expérience de Filippo Sega, légat en France', Classiques Garnier, https://classiques-garnier.com/export/pdf/la-sainte-union-des-catholiques-de-france-et-la-fin-des-guerres-de-religion-1585-1629-la-ligue-et-la-papaute-dans-l-experience-de-filippo-sega-legat-en-france.html (abstract only seen)
not_taken: FAIL: the key is published and already in use on this volume. Outside targets sega1590 (R5612, R5616) and sega1591b (R5615, 82.7% read) read Francia 32 with Meister 1906 key 65, unchanged, validated on the decifrato of 21 Dec 1590 (0.934 vs at most 0.551 for shuffled keys). Lasry's sega1591 (BnF fr. 3613) uses the same key. The ids are not in line/taken-2026-11-19.tsv, but the profile grep for 'Francia 32', 'Sega' and 'R56' finds them. The remaining records R5613-14 and R5617-21 are almost certainly the same key (R5613 view 4 has a 'Decifrato' per Dudout, in the sega1591 profile)
searches: profile grep (sources/cache/bourdeau-profiles-2026-11-19.json); WebSearch 'Filippo Sega nunzio Francia 1590 Dizionario Biografico' (no edition of the 1590-91 despatches). Not checked: DECODE images R5613-14, R5617-21 (login); Lavenia's DBI entry vol. 91
image_url: not checked (DECODE images need a login)
neighbour_keys: Meister 1906 key 65 (Die Geheimschrift im Dienste der päpstlichen Kurie, pp. 435-436), as used in targets/sega1590 and sega1591b; also morosini1588 (Meister no. 40), not the same key
second_passage: yes per the catalogue (ten records of 6-11 pp.)
design: Meister 65: letters as digit pairs, vowels as marks on the digits, nulls, a three-digit nomenclator (per the outside profiles)
failed_gate: not_taken (published key, already applied to the same volume by the outside repo)
notes: If wanted, this is a known-key job for the remaining records (R5613-14, R5617-21), not a key build. The R5613 decifrato would be its held-out check.

image_url: https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item?id=e000875271&op=img&app=nf (6 Nov, ff. 346v-347); pair e000875266-69 (NFA item 27540, https://nouvelle-france.org/eng/item/details?id=27540, ff. 342-345, online)

pair: YES, and online: the 22 Sept cipher letter, ff. 342-343v, with its contemporary decipherment in clear on ff. 344-345 (images e000875268-69), in the same NFA item 27540
pair_signs: by eye about 2 pages x 33 lines x about 8 groups = about 500 code groups (mixed with clear words)
neighbour_keys: none: the Vaudreuil C11E 10 table does not fit (catalogue: 0.063 vs 0.229 shuffled; vaudreuil1760 profile)
second_passage: yes: the 6 Nov letter (about 110 lines, mostly groups). By eye it is the same code: the same groups and stacked fractions recur on both letters (8, 108, 287, 466, 219/466)
design: a numeric code or nomenclator: comma-separated 1-3 digit groups up to about 700, many written as stacked pairs (e.g. 219 over 466), with clear words between runs
failed_gate: readable (5-6 px digit height on 1125 px spreads)
notes: Passes matters and buildable well: a real online pair of about 500 groups plus a 6 Nov passage in the same code. The wall is the image size. What would breach it: ANOM's own scans (IREL / recherche-anom) or a print of the LAC images at higher resolution, not checked. Digit groups may tolerate less than 15 px better than sign shapes do; the calibration was on signs. Coordinate with Dudout before any work.
